title: Microsoft 365 admin center: authoritative SharePoint sites for Copilot Search
summary: The briefing's rollout facts, licensing basis and configuration commands are supported. Minor corrections should complete the SharePoint navigation and acknowledge the cmdlet reference's different wording about which administrator needs a Copilot licence.

claims.claim: The Microsoft 365 Copilot release notes list the admin center feature under 4 November 2026.
claims.quote:
## November 4, 2026
Authoritative content management for Microsoft 365 Copilot Search

claims.claim: Authoritative sites identify official, organisation-managed SharePoint sources whose content Copilot Search recognises as trusted.
claims.quote: Authoritative sites help administrators identify official, organization-managed SharePoint sources. When you mark a site as authoritative, Copilot Search experiences recognize its content as trusted.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Trusted content has visual signals such as the From your organization label.
claims.quote: Visual signals, such as the From your organization label, make trusted items easier to identify.

claims.claim: The SharePoint authoritative sites page directs administrators to PowerShell and CSOM APIs for the current release.
claims.quote: In the current release, configure authoritative sites through PowerShell and CSOM APIs.

claims.claim: The SharePoint authoritative sites page itself gives no admin center designation steps.
claims.quote: Searched: 'SharePoint admin center authoritative sites Mark as authoritative site Active sites'. Read authoritative-sites in full: only PowerShell/CSOM designation procedures. Release notes separately supply UI steps, as the briefing acknowledges.

claims.where: controls[1].note; What's changing; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: Learn does not explicitly identify the admin center list and the PowerShell/CSOM designation as the same list.
claims.quote: Searched: 'SharePoint authoritative sites Microsoft 365 admin center same list CSOM GetAuthoritativeResources'; 'authoritative sites admin center PowerShell list'. Read authoritative-sites, release-notes passages and Set-SPOSite; no explicit equivalence was found.

claims.claim: Microsoft does not explicitly say whether the two documented routes share one 100-site allowance.
claims.quote: Searched: 'SharePoint authoritative sites Microsoft 365 admin center same list CSOM GetAuthoritativeResources'. Opened authoritative-sites and release notes: both state 100 sites, but neither explicitly describes a shared allowance across the routes.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters; Open questions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated the authoritative-content control's default or what happens before sites are designated.
claims.quote: Searched: 'authoritative sites default Copilot Search'. Read roadmap, MC1526676, authoritative-sites, release notes and admin-experience. No initial authoritative list or automatic designation is stated; general Copilot Search availability does not state this control's default.

claims.claim: No source states that this new authoritative-content control automatically changes existing search behaviour before administrator designation.
claims.quote: Searched: 'authoritative sites default Copilot Search'. Read roadmap, MC1526676, authoritative-sites and relevant release-notes passages; these describe administrator designation, not an automatic change to existing search ranking on arrival.

claims.claim: Personal sites cannot be marked authoritative.
claims.quote: Personal sites can't be marked as authoritative.

claims.claim: Running Set-SPOSite requires a SharePoint Online administrator.
claims.quote: You must be a SharePoint Online administrator and be a site collection administrator to run the cmdlet.

claims.claim: The SharePoint Online administrator running Set-SPOSite must also be a site collection administrator.
claims.quote: You must be a SharePoint Online administrator and be a site collection administrator to run the cmdlet.

claims.claim: The documented CSOM workflow registers a Microsoft Entra ID application.
claims.quote:
Step 2: Register a Microsoft Entra ID app
Register an app for interactive authentication and copy the client ID from the output.

claims.claim: The CSOM registration example requests Sites.FullControl.All application permissions.
claims.quote: -SharePointApplicationPermissions "Sites.FullControl.All" -GraphDelegatePermissions "Sites.FullControl.All" -GraphApplicationPermissions "Sites.FullControl.All"

claims.claim: The documented list-management feature does not describe an agent taking autonomous actions.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Copilot Search authoritative autonomous'. Read authoritative-sites, roadmap, MC1526676 and relevant release notes. The feature description covers designation and ranking; the notice's AI/ML-or-agent compliance wording specifies no autonomous action.

claims.claim: Changes can take up to 72 hours to appear in supported experiences.
claims.quote: Changes can take up to 72 hours to appear in supported experiences.

claims.claim: Multi-geo tenants manage authoritative site data per geo.
claims.quote: Multi-geo tenants manage authoritative site data per geo.

claims.claim: The authoritative sites page states that a Microsoft Copilot licence is required.
claims.quote: Licensing: A Microsoft Copilot license is required.

claims.quote:
Prerequisites
See Prerequisites for SharePoint Advanced Management.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Governance guidance; Open questions
claims.claim: The SAM prerequisites grant Copilot-supporting capabilities when at least one organisation user is assigned a Microsoft Copilot licence.
claims.quote: At least one user in your organization is assigned a Microsoft Copilot license. (The user doesn't need to be a SharePoint administrator.)
claims.fix: After the tenant-level licensing statement, add: 'The Set-SPOSite reference instead describes -IsAuthoritative as used by an admin with a Copilot licence; this differs from the tenant-level SAM prerequisite.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/microsoft.online.sharepoint.powershell/set-sposite?view=sharepoint-ps#-isauthoritative. Retain the supported prerequisite statement.

claims.where: Why it matters; Cost and licensing; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Users need an eligible Microsoft Copilot licence to access the Copilot Search experience.
claims.quote: If a user has an eligible Microsoft Copilot license, they can access Copilot Search from the Search module in the Microsoft Copilot app.

claims.claim: Users without an eligible Copilot licence receive the Microsoft Search experience.
claims.quote: Users without an eligible Microsoft Copilot license receive the Microsoft Search experience when they select the Search module in the Microsoft 365 app.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: No separate authoritative-content price is published in the checked Microsoft material.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Copilot Search authoritative sites license pricing meter default IsAuthoritative'. Read authoritative-sites, SAM prerequisites, SAM features in Copilot licenses and Search FAQ excerpt; no authoritative-content-specific price was found.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: No separate authoritative-content meter is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Copilot Search authoritative sites license pricing meter default IsAuthoritative'. Read authoritative-sites, SAM prerequisites, SAM features in Copilot licenses and Search FAQ excerpt; no authoritative-content meter was found. The roadmap names none.

claims.claim: No add-on specific to authoritative content is published.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Copilot Search authoritative sites license pricing meter default IsAuthoritative'. Read authoritative-sites and SAM licensing prerequisites/features. SAM Plan 1 is a general entitlement option; no authoritative-content-specific add-on is named.

claims.claim: The linked SAM prerequisites require an eligible Microsoft 365 or Office 365 base subscription.
claims.quote: Your organization must have one of the following base licenses: Office 365 E3, E5, or A5; Microsoft 365 E1, E3, E5, or A5; Microsoft 365 GCC, GCC-High, or DoD

claims.claim: Authoritative designation is currently site-level only.
claims.quote: Designation is currently site-level only.

claims.claim: Microsoft advises regularly reviewing the list and removing outdated or no-longer-official sites.
claims.quote: Review the list regularly and remove outdated or no-longer-official sites.

claims.claim: Set-SPOSite -Identity <site URL> -IsAuthoritative $true marks the site authoritative using SharePoint Online Management Shell.
claims.quote:
Configure authoritative sites with SharePoint Online Management Shell
Set-SPOSite -Identity "https://<tenant>.sharepoint.com/sites/<siteName>" -IsAuthoritative $true

claims.claim: The 11 August release notes document SharePoint admin center > site > Mark as authoritative site.
claims.quote:
Open the SharePoint admin center.
Select a site and choose 'Mark as authoritative site.'
claims.fix: Expand the path to 'Sites > Active sites > site > Mark as authoritative site'. Add https://learn.microsoft.com/sharepoint/manage-sites-in-new-admin-center to sources; it documents 'Sites > Active sites' then selecting a site. Replace the prose saying full navigation is undocumented with: 'The site-selection navigation is documented on Manage sites in the SharePoint admin center; the designation action is documented in the 11 August 2026 release notes.'

claims.claim: The authoritative sites page documents CSOM operations for bulk designation and removal.
claims.quote:
Bulk mark sites as authoritative
$results = $tenant.BulkSetResourceAsAuthoritative($siteIds)
Bulk remove authoritative sites
$results = $tenant.BulkRemoveResourceAsAuthoritative($siteIds)

claims.claim: The feature's licensing model is included in the named Copilot entitlement rather than a separately documented authoritative-content licence.
claims.quote: If your organization has at least one Microsoft Copilot license assigned to a user, your SharePoint administrators automatically receive access to SharePoint Advanced Management capabilities to support your Copilot deployment.

claims.claim: The Copilot Search admin experience page documents managing bookmarks and acronyms.
claims.quote: For example, you can manage connectors, bookmarks, and acronyms for Copilot Search just as you can for Microsoft Search.

claims.claim: The Copilot Search admin experience page does not cover authoritative content.
claims.quote: Searched: 'authoritative content import format Copilot Search'. Read copilot-search-admin-experience in full; its procedures cover acronyms and bookmarks, not authoritative sites. Read release notes and authoritative-sites for the separately documented feature.

claims.claim: The SharePoint authoritative sites page also limits authoritative designation to 100 sites.
claims.quote: You can mark up to 100 sites as authoritative.

claims.claim: The release notes explicitly say Global admin or Global reader can view, add, delete, and bulk import or export authoritative sites.
claims.quote: Admins with Global admin or Global reader roles can view, add, delete, and bulk import or export up to 100 authoritative SharePoint sites.
